socialTitle: How to Evict a Tenant in New Jersey (2026)

faq.question: Can I evict a tenant in New Jersey without going to court?
faq.answer: No. Every residential eviction in New Jersey requires a judgment for possession and a warrant of removal executed by a court officer. Self-help removal is illegal regardless of what the lease says or how much rent is owed.

faq.question: How long does an eviction take in New Jersey?
faq.answer: Commonly 6 weeks to 3 months from filing for a straightforward nonpayment case, and longer when the case is contested, the tenant obtains a stay, or the ground requires pre-filing notices. County backlogs vary, so treat any estimate as a range.

faq.question: Can I apply the security deposit to unpaid rent during an eviction?
faq.answer: Not unilaterally while the tenancy continues. After the tenant vacates, the deposit is handled under New Jersey's deposit statute, with an itemized accounting due on a 30-day deadline — see our security deposit guide for the rules.
